doc.title: Sol Yaged interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000

title: Sweet By and By's end and Goodman playing Gershwin in Philadelphia
summary: Sol skipped work at the Metropole to hear Goodman in Philadelphia.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: It was gorgeous. And she sang this sexy song called “Low and Lazy.” Then he used the song again at the second part of the show with a beat and he called it “Crisp and Crunchy.” The same song with a beat. It was so intelligent what he did. And I don’t know, I may still have the music for this show. The name of the show was called “Sweet By and By.” It was written by S.J. Perelman, music by Vernon Duke. I wonder if I still have that music. “Crisp and Crunchy,” and “Low and Lazy.” [Sol plays]. Oh boy, you can’t beat George Gershwin. Benny Goodman played with the Philadelphia Symphony for one day, a medley of George Gershwin songs which I tried to play for you right now, Monk, where he started off with the “Rhapsody in Blue.” We’re going back to the early 1950s, ’50, ’51. In fact I was working at The Metropole then come to think of it, and I took off. The owner, Ben Harriman, was very upset with me that I took off. I told him, “I want to go see Benny Goodman.” He said, “where’s he playing?” He thought he was playing in the city where I could hear him and then come back to work. I says, “no, he’s playing at the Academy of Music in Philadelphia.” He says, “you’re going all the way out there to see and hear Ben—” I says, “yes.” Anyhow he played this “Rhapsody in Blue” with this Philadelphia Symphony. They did a medley of George Gershwin’s songs, like “Someone to Watch Over Me,” and “Embraceable You,” and then he ended up with “The Man I Love.” It was so beautiful it actually brought tears to my eyes. He played it like a classical, like with strings. Like he would play [Sol plays]. And then the last piece he did with the orchestra was [Sol plays]. That’s what he did. He went down the low register, it was just beautiful. I’m going back 45 years ago. And I’ll never forget that concert, my dear friend. And he did this with the symphony orchestra, a medley of George Gershwin songs. It was gorgeous. I’m sorry if I’m boring you my dear friend.
